title: Private Type Representation Leaked in Headers
pattern: Declaring private layout structures or low-level primitives in public class fields or header files, exposing internal representation details to clients.
why_bad: Client code becomes tightly coupled to the specific container or representation (e.g., using String instead of an Address type). Changing the representation later breaks compile-compatibility for all clients.
detection: A header file exposes low-level primitive types or private data fields in its public API contract instead of abstract interface wrappers.
counterexample: Using private implementation pointer wrappers (the Pimpl idiom) or abstract interfaces to hide internal structure details.
fix: Encapsulate the internal type using private variables and expose abstract interfaces or dedicated wrapper types.
